item.title: Tinubu seeks Senate confirmation of NMDPRA executive directors, board secretary
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has urged the Senate to confirm the appointments of Executive Directors and Secretary of the Board of Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority (NMDPRA). Tinubu’s request is contained in a letter addressed to the Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, and read at plenary on Tuesday. Tinubu, in the letter, said the appointments were made in accordance with the provisions of Section 41, Subsections 2 and 3 of Petroleum Industry Act, 2021. He listed the nominees for reappointment to include Mr Abiodun Adeniji, Executive Director, Finance and Accounts and Mr Ogbugo Ukoha, Executive Director, Distribution Systems, Storage and Retailing Infrastructure. Dr Mustapha Lamode, the Executive Director, Health, Safety, Environment and Community, was also listed for reappointment. Tinubu also listed the nominees for new appointments to include Mr Mobolaji Musa as Executive Director, Hydrocarbon Processing Plants, Installation and Partnership and Ms Ogechukwu Modie as Executive Director, Economic Regulation and Strategic Planning. Others are Mr Said Abutali as Executive Director, Corporate Services and Administration, and Mrs Jumoke Gafar as Board Secretary and Legal Adviser. The President expressed the hope that the senate would consider and confirm the nominees in its usual expeditious manner. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Akpabio, thereafter, referred the letter to the Committees on Petroleum Resources (Downstream) and Petroleum Resources (Gas) for further legislative inputs and to revert to plenary within one week. item.title: Anthropic Targets Valuation Of Up To $1.4 Trillion
item.description: Anthropic plans to raise up to $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering, the artificial intelligence giant said in a filing Tuesday, putting the company’s total valuation at up to $1.4 trillion. The maker of AI agent Claude said in a filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission that it aims to sell 825 million shares of Class A common stock at a Wall Street debut price estimate of “between $70.00 and $78.00” per share, amounting to $64.3 billion. Anthropic had been expected to raise up to $100 billion in its IPO, which would have made it the largest IPO on record. The stock market debut is being seen as a gauge of how long the AI spending boom lifting the US economy can last. And it comes as Wall Street is busy digesting the impact of the US midterm elections, in which Democrats won majority control of both chambers of Congress and are vowing to put the brakes on President Donald Trump’s agenda. Anthropic has been aiming to hold its initial public offering the week of November 16. This photograph shows the logo of the US artificial intelligence safety and research company Anthropic displayed on a smartphone’s screen in Brussels on June 10, 2026. Photo by NICOLAS TUCAT / AFP On Monday, the company announced it would release updated versions of two of its most powerful AI models, Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, which it said can perform 30 percent faster than previous versions. Growth has been staggering at the company. Anthropic’s revenue reached $17 billion in the third quarter, up from just $1.4 billion a year earlier, a securities filing showed earlier this month. On Tuesday, the company said its annualized projection, known as the run-rate revenue, “was approximately $81 billion as of October 31, 2026, up $10 billion from September 30.” Estimates in recent months had forecast Anthropic’s valuation at up to a staggering $2 trillion, but the estimates have slipped along with a slide in AI stock prices on Wall Street. Several US media outlets, including The Wall Street Journal and The New York Times on Tuesday estimated the valuation of the company at between $1.3 trillion and $1.4 trillion. item.title: 2027: Duke seeks opposition unity as PRP unveils manifesto
item.description: Presidential candidate of People’s Redemption Party (PRP), Mr Donald Duke, on Tuesday in Abuja unveiled his ‘A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal’ manifesto. Duke, at the occasion, urged opposition parties to bridge their differences, not for personal ambition, but to safeguard the nation’s democratic foundations. He warned that repeating what he called the miscalculations of the 2023 elections in 2027 would bring ‘lasting shame’. “We erred in 2023, and we are repeating the same in 2027. It is said, Fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us,” he remarked. Duke called for an unconventional tactical thinking among opposition forces to counter what he termed an ‘unguarded political establishment’. “David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he stated. While building on the party’s strategic outlook, PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, said the occasion served as a vital vehicle to transition the party from mere aspirations to governing reality. Baba-Ahmed praised the party’s presidential candidate and his running mate, Malam Sule Mohammed, alongside more than 500 other candidates. He described them as models of integrity, competence and courage designed to lead the nation out of its current economic and security quagmire. The national chairman acknowledged the immense challenges that plagued the party, including competing against incumbent politicians who relied on state power and immense financial resources. “We will find resistance from politicians who bribe our people for our future, while we ask for trust and the courage to choose quality and integrity,” he said. He also urged supporters to reject vote-buying, declaring, “Nigeria and Nigerians are not for sale. Baba-Ahmed outlined the party’s commitment to historic reforms, including what he termed a groundbreaking initiative that required all candidates to sign a binding compact with their constituents. “This agreement commits aspirants to unprecedented accountability, service and adherence to the foundational values of the 70-year-old progressive movement,” he said. While emphasising the party’s active role in the emerging Coalition for Democracy, Baba-Ahmed urged candidates to reject ‘politics as usual’ and campaign with sincerity, respect and an unwavering dedication to national redemption. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Duke, in an interview with newsmen shortly after the programme, also spoke on the state of the judiciary and the viability of an opposition coalition. item.title: 2027: Study our manifesto, judge us by promises kept – Presidency tells Nigerians
item.description: …As APC-PCC unveils 4-point manifesto, 8 priority areas By Soni Daniel (Editor, North), Emma Ujah (Bureau Chief, Abuja) & Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA The Presidency has urged Nigerians to study the past and current manifestoes of the ruling All Progressives Congress APC and judge the party by the promises it has kept since 2023, when it assumed power. The Chief of Staff to President Bola Tinubu, Hon. Femi Gbajabiamila, gave the charge on Tuesday in Abuja at the unveiling of the APC manifesto, titled ‘From Reforms to Prosperity’. He described the manifesto as a binding pact with the electorate. “A manifesto, in its strictest sense, is simply a contract between the people and their leaders. It is an inviolable contract, and we take the strict interpretation of what a manifesto represents as gospel under this administration,” he said. He admitted that the reforms had put real pressure on households, adding that the people living through it deserve to be heard. “Nobody should have to pretend that life is easy at the moment,” he said. The former House Speaker nonetheless defended President Bola Tinubu’s decision to act, saying Tinubu confronted the subsidy burden and a distorted foreign exchange system when he took responsibility for the country in 2023. “Leaving those problems untouched would have continued to weaken our ability to invest in the future. The difference between a politician and a leader is that while a politician thinks about the next election, a leader thinks about the next generation. And that is exactly what President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has demonstrated,” Gbajabiamila said. 4 pillars The manifesto rests on four pillars: a secure and resilient nation; a better quality and more affordable life for every Nigerian; energy, infrastructure and economic growth; and effective and accountable governance. They are tied to the eight priority areas of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which the document says will be carried out on four foundations: macroeconomic stability, the rule of law, institutional capability and national cohesion. By 2031, the document commits to power generation scaled towards 10,000 megawatts, annual economic growth of 6 per cent, and youth unemployment and out-of-school children both halved. It also promises 20,000 additional teachers and health insurance expanded from more than 23 million enrollees to 40 per cent of Nigerians. It further promises to work towards 200,000 homes under the Tinubu Mass Social Housing Scheme, Federal Mortgage Bank of Nigeria (FMBN) mortgages and licensed private developers, tracked on a public dashboard. item.title: Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO
item.description: Cholera has killed more than 3,000 people worldwide since the start of the year, the World Health Organization said Tuesday, insisting its goal of cutting global cases by 90 percent by 2030 remained in reach. The disease killed nearly 7,900 people in 2025, making it “the deadliest year for cholera since 1999”, according to Lorenzo Pezzoli, WHO lead for epidemic-prone bacterial diseases. While data for the first nine months of 2026 show a decline in deaths, more than 3,000 people have still died from the preventable and treatable diarrheal infection, he said, with “nearly nine out of 10 of them in Africa”. The WHO also warned that the current El Nino weather pattern could worsen outbreaks, as cholera can be fuelled by both flooding and water shortages. The UN health agency and the vaccine alliance, Gavi, aim to reduce global cholera cases by 90 percent by 2030 through mass vaccination campaigns and improved access to clean water and sanitation. Although cholera was eliminated from high-income countries generations ago thanks to safe drinking water and modern sewage systems, it can still “kill within a matter of hours” if left untreated, Pezzoli said, despite being “easy and inexpensive to treat” with existing medicines. “The 2030 goal is achievable because the work is already under way,” Pezzoli added, pointing to the International Coordinating Group (ICG) on Vaccine Provision, which last year approved the supply of 71 million doses, funded by Gavi. Vaccines and rapid diagnostic tests are also reaching outbreak zones more quickly, helping health workers detect and respond to infections earlier. WHO and its partners are helping countries identify districts where cholera repeatedly resurfaces and develop response plans. Seven countries — Angola, Bangladesh, the DR Congo, Nigeria, South Sudan, Sudan and Yemen — accounted for about 90 percent of global cases and deaths last year. “The collective response is undeniably bearing fruit, but… it remains insufficient,” Pezzoli said. “We must redouble our efforts to help all these countries reach the elimination goal which means ensuring that, by 2030, cholera no longer poses a public health threat in any of them.” The post Cholera killed more than 3,000 this year – WHO appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Senate donates N100m to Nigeria’s U-17 women’s team, Flamingos
item.description: The Senate has announced a donation of N100 million to Nigeria’s Under-17 women’s national football team, the Flamingos, following their historic victory at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Rabat, Morocco. The Senate President announced the donation during plenary on Tuesday while presiding over a motion moved by Sen. Abdul Ningi (ADC-Bauchi Central) on the need to congratulate the victorious girls on their achievement. Ningi described the victory as historic, noting that the young players had achieved what several other Nigerian national teams had struggled to accomplish. He said the team’s triumph was particularly remarkable, given the limited expectations that surrounded the players before the competition. The senator expressed concern that the achievement had not received adequate publicity and national recognition, adding that the players deserved to be celebrated for bringing honour to Nigeria and Africa. He also expressed concern that the team did not receive sufficient official recognition upon its arrival in the country. Seconding the motion, Sen. Adams Oshiomhole (APC-Edo North) commended the team for defeating Japan in the final, describing the victory as evidence of the potential and determination of Nigerian youths. Oshiomhole urged Nigerians to appreciate the country’s achievements rather than constantly focusing on its challenges. He also appealed to the Senate leadership to make a donation to the team to support the players’ educational needs alongside their sporting careers. The senate thereafter adopted Ningi’s prayers, congratulating President Bola Tinubu for his support for sports development, Nigerians on the historic victory, and the leadership of the National Sports Commission, particularly its Chairman, Shehu Dikko. It also urged the federal government to provide adequate compensation and rewards for the players in recognition of their achievement. Senate President, Godswill Akpabio, in his remarks, said the victory was a significant achievement for Nigeria and Africa, particularly as the Flamingos defeated football nations, including Brazil and Japan. Akpabio urged the federal government to adequately reward the players and called on the Nigeria Football Federation (NFF) to sustain the team and continue developing the players for future competitions. The senate president also appealed to wealthy and sports-loving Nigerians to support the players and encourage other young people to participate in sports. item.title: US university suspends fraternity after students filmed on fire
item.description: Ohio State University in the United States has suspended a fraternity after footage emerged showing two young men on fire, local media reported on Monday. The video, which garnered more than 1.5 million views on X, shows the pair surrounded by a group laughing and filming as they roll around on the ground, engulfed in flames. Fraternities — male social clubs common on US campuses — have long come under scrutiny for booze-infused parties and hazing rituals that can lead to sexual assault, accidents and even deaths. The elite Cornell University suspended fraternity parties and social events last month for the remaining academic year following an alleged gang rape at one of its clubs that has horrified Americans. “The university is aware of this extremely concerning incident, and the individuals in question are receiving needed medical care,” Ohio State University spokesman Ben Johnson said in a statement quoted by local news outlet WCMH-TV. “Ohio State has placed the Sigma Alpha Epsilon fraternity on interim suspension pending a full investigation.” Sigma Alpha Epsilon claims on its website to have “forged men into leaders” since its foundation in 1856. Columbus police said they were also investigating the incident. The post US university suspends fraternity after students filmed on fire appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Escalating CNG Prices: FG Threatens Sanctions Against Marketers Exploiting Unsuspecting Nigerians
item.description: The Federal Government has threatened to sanction marketers exploiting unsuspecting Nigerians over escalating prices of Compressed Natural Gas (CNG) across the country. Minister of State for Petroleum Resources (Gas), Ekperikpe Ekpo, spoke on Tuesday in Kano during the inspection of some CNG mother station infrastructure ahead of the commissioning of the Abuja-Kaduna-Kano AKK Pipeline and opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily. Ekpo during the opening of two CNG daughter stations capable of dispensing CNG to more than 2,500 vehicles and 50 trucks daily in Kano, on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. He said that the days of those exploiting Nigerian’s by taking advantage of the federal government’s CNG programme to acquire kits, buy CNG, and still charge unsuspecting Nigerians the same as those using petrol will soon be over. According to him, the goal is to flood the country with more CNG stations to meet the current high demand and encourage even more Nigerians, especially commercial drivers, to convert their vehicles. The minister also urged those alleging that the process of obtaining funds for CNG infrastructure expansion from the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund was not transparent and almost impossible. He challenged them to back such claims with evidence, adding that those who have complied with all the requirements have accessed the funds. item.title: Meet only two countries to have won both men’s, women’s U-20 World Cups
item.description: Germany and Spain are the only two countries to have won both the FIFA U-20 Men’s World Cup and the FIFA U-20 Women’s World Cup. The two European nations have achieved the feat by winning titles in both competitions, which showcase some of the world’s best emerging football talents. Germany became the first to accomplish the double, with its men’s team, then competing as West Germany, winning the U-20 World Cup in 1981. The country’s women’s team subsequently claimed the U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2004, 2010 and 2014, taking its tally to three titles in the competition. Spain also joined the exclusive list after winning the men’s U-20 World Cup in 1999, when the tournament was hosted by Nigeria. The Spanish men’s team defeated Japan 4-0 in the final in Lagos to secure its first title. More than two decades later, Spain’s women’s team won its maiden U-20 Women’s World Cup in 2022, defeating Japan 3-1 in the final in Costa Rica. Spain added a second women’s title in 2026, further strengthening its record across both competitions. The achievement places Germany and Spain in a select group of countries that have conquered both sides of FIFA’s U-20 World Cup competitions. item.title: Obi will run to Cameroon if confronted with burdens of presidency – Wike
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, Abuja Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has accused the presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, of lacking the capacity to tackle the myriads of Nigeria’s challenges but would instead flee to Cameroon if handed the responsibilities of the presidency. Wike spoke on Tuesday at the Abaji Area Council Rainbow Coalition and Stakeholders’ Meeting in Abuja, where he urged FCT residents to back President Bola Tinubu’s re-election bid in 2027. He said Obi would run away from the country’s problems instead of tackling them headlong, unlike Tinubu, whom he praised for taking difficult decisions. According to the minister, Nigeria needs a president who can confront hard situations and not abandon the country when challenges arise. He argued that the presidency is not a position for political theatrics or public relations but one that demands courage, capacity and the willingness to take responsibility. Wike asked the Abaji leaders to prove their support for Tinubu at the polls. He warned political leaders against making promises they cannot fulfil and said he would judge them by their ability to deliver their wards for the President in 2027. “Let me repeat what I said yesterday. To the people of Abaji, through their chairman, councillors and leaders, you come from different wards. You have told me you will vote for Tinubu. I have no problem with that. I want to see it,” he said. He specifically charged the Abaji Area Council chairman and other leaders to secure victory for Tinubu in their wards, stressing that leadership must be shown through electoral results. The minister said the FCT must not only match Rivers State in electoral performance but surpass it, adding that he was ready to apply the same political mobilisation strategy in Abuja. “Nobody is competing with Rivers. I don’t know what you all think. The only people who are going to compete with Rivers are the FCT. Whatever I will do there, I will do it here. So make sure you beat Rivers,” Wike said. Wike also cautioned residents against repeating what he described as the mistake of the 2023 elections, when they allegedly voted for candidates who did not keep in touch with their constituents after winning. “You went and elected somebody you don’t know. Is it not correct? Have you seen the person again? Has he come to address you? Has he asked you what your problems are? Has he moved anything that will affect the interest of the FCT?” he asked. The minister disclosed that he would meet FCT youths on Wednesday to discuss political mobilisation and other issues affecting their participation in the forthcoming elections. He assured stakeholders that the resources and arrangements for the electioneering campaign were being put in place and expressed confidence in the readiness of the Rainbow Coalition to mobilise support for Tinubu. item.title: Ogun Gov Poll: PDP candidate’s name not in party’s register, INEC tells court
item.description: … as LP chieftain alleges plot to compromise judge By Ikechukwu Nnochiri ABUJA — The Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) has explained to the Federal High Court in Abuja why it excluded Ogun State PDP candidate Mr Ladi Adebutu from its list of candidates cleared for the 2027 general elections. In a counter-affidavit deposed to by Mr Mustapha Mohammed, a Chief Program Analyst in its Information and Communication Technology (ICT) Department, the Commission told the court that Adebutu’s name was not found in the register of members the PDP earlier submitted to it. It told the court that it found only the name of the PDP’s deputy governorship candidate in the state, Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi, in the register. INEC’s counter-affidavit was in opposition to a suit marked FHC/ABJ/CS/2573/2026, which the PDP and its Ogun State governorship candidate, Adebutu, filed against it. While the PDP is the 1st plaintiff in the matter, Adebutu is listed as the 2nd plaintiff, with INEC named as the sole defendant. It will be recalled that INEC had omitted Adebutu’s name from the final list of 13 candidates cleared to contest the Ogun State governorship election billed for February 6, 2027. Dissatisfied with the action, the PDP approached the court for an order compelling INEC to reverse its decision by recognising Adebutu’s candidacy. However, in the process it filed to challenge the competence of the suit, INEC said it had done due diligence before the final list of candidates for the election was published. According to the deponent, “I know as a fact that before the Governorship Candidates Final List was published, the ICT department conducted a search on the membership register submitted by the 1st plaintiff and during the search, the ICT department found the name of the 1st plaintiff’s candidate fielded as Deputy Governor of Ogun State (Kolapo Lateefat Oyeyemi) in the register but could not find the name of the 2nd plaintiff. “The search was also conducted to find a possible match for the name of the 2nd plaintiff, but no possible match was found in the Ogun State membership register. “That I know as a fact that all the queries conducted on the membership register in the flash drives (PDF/read only) submitted to the defendant by the 1st plaintiff do not contain the name of the 2nd plaintiff. “That the flash drive attached to the plaintiff’s affidavit and further affidavit in support of the Originating Summons was shown to me and I have carefully examined it, and I state that the contents of the flash drive are not the same as those submitted to the defendant. “That the first flash drive submitted by the 1st plaintiff to the defendant on 22 April 2026 had files named Ogun 01-038, while the second flash drive submitted to the defendant had files named Ogun 01-04, with serial numbers of members 1–18,973 and 1–19,308 respectively. “That serial number 1536 on the membership register submitted by the 1st plaintiff to the defendant contains the name of one

item.title: Kompany returns to Bayern’s training ground for first time since collapse
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany returned to the club’s training ground on Tuesday for the first time since collapsing last month, beginning a gradual return to work ahead of the Bundesliga match against Cologne on November 20. The 40-year-old was at Bayern’s Säbener Straße complex shortly after 10am, according to German media reports. He worked from his office, spoke with assistant coach Floribert Ngalula and sporting director Christoph Freund, and watched injured players complete a recovery session. His return to the training ground does not mean he has resumed all his duties, as he is expected back in the dugout after the international break. Kompany collapsed on October 23 while watching a training session involving Bayern’s reserve team. He was hospitalised and diagnosed with meningeal irritation, an inflammation affecting the tissue around the brain or spinal cord. He was later discharged to recover at home. Assistant Aaron Danks took charge during Kompany’s absence, overseeing four wins and a 2-2 draw with Borussia Dortmund. Bayern beat Freiburg, Magdeburg, Atlético Madrid and Mainz. Danks said the club had instructed him to keep football discussions away from Kompany while he recovered. “I have clear instructions from Max [Eberl] and Christoph [Freund] not to engage in discussions, first of all, and to keep Vince focused on nothing other than his health and spending time with his family,” he said. “We want him to rest and recover properly so that, when he returns, he is fully fit and can help us in the best possible way. We are being very strict here and keeping football completely out of it.” Kompany’s father, Pierre, had previously described his son’s demanding work routine in an interview with Bild. “He works 18 hours a day most days and, on a typical day, barely sees his children,” he said, adding that Kompany was often at the training ground early and left late. Bayern are scheduled to host Cologne on November 20, when Kompany is expected to return to the touchline. item.title: 2027: Nnaji vows to end excessive taxation in Enugu
item.description: By Ugochukwu Alaribe UMUAHIA — The governorship candidate of the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) in Enugu State, Chief Uche Nnaji, has said he is contesting the 2027 election to rescue the state from what he described as excessive taxation and its impact on businesses and residents. Nnaji alleged that the high tax burden was forcing businessmen and investors to relocate from the state, adding that Enugu had become one of the most expensive places to do business in the country. He spoke while addressing indigenes of Enugu State resident in Aba, Abia State, under the umbrella of the Enugu State Consultative Forum, Abia State chapter. The former Minister of Science and Technology pledged to revive the state’s economy through industrialisation, job creation and measures to address insecurity and unemployment. He said he had been consulting Enugu indigenes living outside the state to draw their attention to what he described as the challenges facing the state and seek their support ahead of the election. Nnaji expressed concern over what he described as the return of armed robbery in parts of Enugu, attributing the development to unemployment, hunger and economic hardship. He promised to establish industries that would create employment opportunities, reduce poverty and take more than 50,000 youths off the streets. “What is happening in Enugu State is condemnable. Enugu is for all, but today, businessmen and investors are relocating from the state due to excessive taxation. And the state government doesn’t care. “Our people are suffering from excessive taxation, even in the rural areas. Traders in rural communities only open their businesses in the evening when tax officials have left. Government collects N36,000 from traders in the villages, when most of them do not make such an amount annually. “Tax is based on profit, not on shops, as they are doing in Enugu. People are hungry. Armed people now invade homes at midnight to collect phones, computers and food items such as rice, beans and garri. This is something that happened more than 20 years ago,” he said. The PDP candidate also questioned the state’s internally generated revenue (IGR), claiming that it had risen from N26 billion to N406.7 billion. He compared the figure with the revenue generated by Abia and Anambra states, arguing that the high revenue collection raised questions about the state’s taxation policies and their impact on businesses. Nnaji further alleged that Enugu’s debt profile had increased significantly under the current administration, although he did not provide figures to substantiate the claim. He said government should focus on creating wealth and improving the living conditions of residents rather than imposing taxes that could undermine businesses. “We have set up the Enugu State Recovery Committee, with me as chairman. item.title: Police confirm escape of two convicted inmates from Kogi prison
item.description: By Boluwaji Obahopo, Lokoja The Kogi State Police Command has confirmed the escape of two convicted inmates from the Okene Correctional Centre, saying efforts are underway to apprehend them. The Police Public Relations Officer in the state, ASP Saliu Oyiza Afusat, disclosed this in a statement issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. According to Afusat, the inmates escaped from the correctional facility on Sunday, November 8, at about 10:30 a.m. She said the command received a report from the correctional centre and was collaborating with the Nigerian Correctional Service and other relevant security agencies to ensure the prompt rearrest of the escapees. The police spokesperson added that efforts to trace and apprehend the fleeing inmates were ongoing. Afusat also clarified that the statement was her first and only official communication to the press on the incident. She urged members of the public to disregard any other information or publication attributed to her on the matter unless officially confirmed by the police command. item.title: 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway pileup
item.description: Eleven people died and dozens were injured on Tuesday in a mass pileup on a motorway in southeastern Bulgaria, whose roads rank as the most dangerous in the EU. Crashes in thick fog snared dozens of vehicles heading in both directions of the highway linking the capital Sofia to the Black Sea city of Burgas. An estimated 50 cars and trucks were involved in the accident near the city of Yambol, regional governor Georgi Chalakov told the BTA state news agency, as government officials rushed to the scene. Images showed overturned and smashed cars and trucks mangled together, as well as burnt-out vehicles. “The toll at this point is 11 dead and 48 injured,” Prime Minister Rumen Radev told reporters. Radev was meeting EU chief Ursula von der Leyen, who is on a visit to Bulgaria, but the prime minister cancelled his official events scheduled for later Tuesday. The injured were transported to hospitals in nearby cities. The government dispatched two aircraft equipped with stretchers and medical teams. Bulgaria saw 71 road fatalities per million inhabitants in 2025, the highest rate in the European Union, according to European Commission figures. Victims blame the Balkan nation’s high number of traffic deaths on reckless driving, poorly maintained roads and an inefficient justice system. Stricter penalties Romanian Foreign Minister Dan Neculaescu said one Romanian was among the injured and expressed “deepest condolences” to the victims and their families in a post on X. European Council chief Antonio Costa also said on X he was “deeply saddened to learn of the tragic traffic accident in Bulgaria this morning”. A total of 456 people were killed in road traffic accidents in Bulgaria in 2025 — down five percent from the previous year and 27 percent lower than in 2019. The EU in 2019 introduced a target to reduce road deaths and serious injuries by 50 percent by 2030. A European Commission report in October said that although the EU remains “one of the world’s safest regions for road travel”, the majority of member states were not yet on track to meet the safety target. The report said that just five of the EU’s 27 countries — including Bulgaria — were on track to meet the target. However, “despite their progress since 2019, Bulgaria and Romania, alongside Croatia, continue to have the highest fatality rates in the EU when measuring deaths per million inhabitants”, the report said. In 2023, Bulgaria’s parliament adopted stricter penalties for anyone found to be driving under the influence of drugs. The cars of accused drivers are now impounded until the trial, even when the suspects have no previous criminal record. Bulgaria’s busy road traffic due to its position as a gateway to the EU is one of the main factors behind the high accident rate, according to experts. But Bulgaria’s status as the EU’s poorest member state also plays a role, with around half of the cars registered more than 20 years old. Vanguard News The post 11 dead, dozens injured in motorway

item.title: Only 36% of Nigerians have access to improved toilets — FG
item.description: By Folarin Kehinde The Federal Government has disclosed that less than 36 per cent of Nigerians have access to improved toilet facilities, raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges and the associated public health risks. The Minister of Environment, Balarabe Abbas Lawal, disclosed this on Tuesday during a press briefing in Abuja to commemorate the 2026 World Toilet Day. Lawal, who was represented by the Director of Pollution Control and Environmental Health, Mrs Omotunde Adeola, said many public places, including markets, motor parks, schools and communities, still lacked adequate and functional toilet facilities. He warned that the situation was contributing to open defecation, contamination of food and water sources, and the spread of sanitation-related diseases such as cholera and typhoid. According to him, inadequate sanitation poses serious threats to public health, environmental safety and human dignity. The minister said women, girls, children, older persons and persons living with disabilities were particularly affected by the shortage of appropriate sanitation facilities. He stressed that no child should miss school because of inadequate toilet facilities, while no woman or girl should be forced to compromise her safety and dignity because of the absence of suitable toilets. Providing a global perspective, Lawal said about 4.5 billion people worldwide still lacked safely managed sanitation, while 892 million continued to practise open defecation. He said the figures underscored the need to accelerate efforts towards achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, particularly those relating to clean water and sanitation, gender equality, good health and sustainable communities by 2030. Government interventions On efforts to address the challenge, the minister said the Federal Ministry of Environment, in collaboration with relevant ministries, state governments and development partners, was implementing programmes to improve sanitation and promote safe excreta disposal nationwide. He listed the initiatives to include capacity building for Environmental Health Officers on faecal sludge management and toilet design, the Clean and Green Programme, and the Community-Based Waste Management and Open Defecation Control Programme. Other interventions, he said, included integrating sanitation into climate adaptation and circular economy initiatives, as well as partnering with private sector operators to provide environmentally friendly sanitation facilities. Lawal announced that the ministry would convene a National Dialogue on Faecal Sludge Management on November 23, 2026, involving seven selected states across the six geopolitical zones and the Federal Capital Territory. He said the dialogue would enable participating states to assess their experiences, share challenges and develop practical recommendations for improving faecal sludge management. item.title: MOSOP accuses Niger Delta governors of mismanaging 13% derivation funds
item.description: ….Group calls for amendment of derivation law, commends NDDC’s development efforts By Daniel Abia PORT HARCOURT — The Movement for the Survival of the Ogoni People (MOSOP) has accused successive governors in the Niger Delta of mismanaging the 13 per cent derivation funds, calling for an amendment of the law to ensure that oil-producing communities directly benefit from the revenue. MOSOP President, Fegalo Nsuke, made the call on Tuesday in Port Harcourt during activities marking the 31st anniversary of the execution of environmental activist Ken Saro-Wiwa and eight other Ogoni leaders by the military government of the late General Sani Abacha. Nsuke said the objectives of the derivation fund had not been achieved because state governors allegedly exercised excessive discretion over its allocation, rather than directing the resources to communities where oil and gas were extracted. He argued that the sacrifices of Saro-Wiwa and other Ogoni martyrs would have limited impact on the lives of people unless laws governing resource benefits specifically addressed the needs of communities bearing the consequences of oil exploration. “The idea of derivation funds was to address the underdevelopment in the Niger Delta region. However, the structure of administration of the funds makes it vulnerable to abuse and has left the funds at the discretion of state governors. This needs to be addressed,” he said. According to Nsuke, the intention behind the derivation arrangement was to address underdevelopment in oil-producing areas, but the funds were not being adequately directed towards those communities. Citing Ogba/Egbema and Andoni communities in Rivers State, he said areas responsible for significant oil production had yet to receive what he considered adequate development funding. He argued that allowing governors to determine spending priorities without directly channelling an appropriate share to oil-producing communities had undermined the objectives of the derivation arrangement. Commends NDDC Despite his criticism of the management of derivation funds, Nsuke commended the current management of the Niger Delta Development Commission (NDDC) for what he described as its visible development impact across the region. He urged the commission to sustain and expand its interventions, noting that the agency emerged from the struggles for justice and development championed by Saro-Wiwa and other Niger Delta activists. “It is important that the areas from where resources are extracted should get their due rewards and a proportionate injection of the derivation funds. The structure for the administration of the derivation funds needs to change if we must achieve that. “I am pleased that the NDDC under its present management is making some impressive impacts. MOSOP will encourage them to do more,” he said. item.title: Troops rescue three kidnap victims, kill two terrorists in Adamawa
item.description: By Kingsley Omonobi Troops of Operation Hadin Kai (OPHK) have rescued three kidnapped civilians and killed two terrorists in separate operations in Adamawa State. The troops also recovered two AK-47 rifles, ammunition, locally fabricated explosive devices, stolen vehicles and farm produce belonging to residents who narrowly escaped abduction. The Acting Media Information Officer of OPHK, Capt. Mohammed Goni, disclosed this in a statement on Tuesday. He said the three victims were rescued by troops deployed in Mubi following a distress call from farmers around Dutse-Uku in Mubi South Local Government Area. According to him, suspected kidnappers abducted a farmer, identified as Happiness Dama Dauda, on November 9 while she was working on her farm and also stole her motorcycle. Goni said the troops, working with local hunters, mobilised to the area and mounted pressure on the kidnappers, forcing them to abandon their victim and flee. He added that a sustained pursuit led to the rescue of two other residents suspected to have been abducted earlier, bringing the number of rescued victims to three. The troops also recovered a motorcycle, a tricycle conveying 15 bags of beans and a Hi-Jet pickup carrying 13 bags of groundnuts belonging to other farmers who narrowly escaped abduction. Goni said the respective village heads identified the recovered items, which were subsequently handed over to their owners. Two terrorists killed in Gombi In a separate operation on November 8, troops deployed at Zangula Kilba Junction in Gombi Local Government Area foiled an attempted attack by suspected Boko Haram/Islamic State West Africa Province (ISWAP) terrorists. Two terrorists were killed during the encounter, while others fled following what the military described as the troops’ superior combat readiness and tactical resilience. Items recovered from the fleeing insurgents included two AK-47 rifles, four magazines, 115 rounds of ammunition, three belts of empty ammunition links and two cases of locally fabricated explosive devices. Other recovered items included a pair of desert boots, a backpack, an Android phone, a wristwatch and N15,000. Goni said troops had commenced exploitation operations to track down the fleeing terrorists and prevent them from regrouping. He added that troops were maintaining aggressive patrols and surveillance across the affected areas to prevent further attacks and reassure residents of their safety. The military urged residents to provide timely and credible intelligence to security agencies, stressing that collaboration between troops and local communities remained critical to tackling terrorism and other security threats. Operation Hadin Kai reaffirmed its commitment to sustaining operational pressure on terrorists and their collaborators to deny them the freedom to threaten the security and livelihoods of residents across the North-East. item.title: Madonna University: 15 nursing students beg for expulsion, suspension reversal over TikTok video
item.description: By Chioma Okoye Fifteen nursing students of Madonna University, Nigeria, have appealed to the university management to reverse their expulsion and suspension over a controversial TikTok video recorded during their community posting, pleading for another opportunity to complete their studies. The students, in a letter dated November 2, 2026, tendered an unreserved apology to the management, admitting that their conduct was unethical and had brought disrepute to the nursing profession and the university community. The video, which went viral on social media, sparked widespread reactions and prompted disciplinary action by the university management. In the appeal addressed to the university management through the Registrar, the students said they had reflected deeply on their actions and were genuinely remorseful. “We sincerely regret our said actions and assure the University Management and all relevant authorities that such an incident will not repeat itself again,” they said. They pleaded with the management to reconsider its decision, stressing that their families had made significant sacrifices to support their education and enable them to reach the present stage of their academic journey. The students said reversing the expulsion would give them an opportunity to complete their programmes and pursue their chosen professional careers instead of having their academic aspirations cut short. They also appreciated the university management for engaging with their parents and guardians and allowing them to present their concerns. According to the students, they did not take the gesture for granted and remained grateful for the opportunity given to their families to be heard. The appeal, jointly signed by the 15 students, urged the university management to reconsider the punishment and give them a second chance. item.title: Tinubu’s achievements will make it difficult to unseat him – Wike
item.description: The Minister of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), Mr Nyesom Wike, says it will be immensely difficult for opposition parties to unseat President Bola Tinubu in the upcoming 2027 general elections. Wike said this in Abuja on Tuesday, after inspecting some ongoing projects within the federal capital territory. He cited what he described as Tinubu’s undeniable and rich report card of infrastructure development across the country. The minister said that the volume and pace of visible achievements delivered under Tinubu’s administration left very little room for political detractors to challenge the ruling party’s record. “You can see clearly that it will be difficult to unseat the president today because the report card is obvious in terms of what he has done. “Like I told you, this is our campaign. People ask what we are going to campaign with, but we have so many visible achievements all around us. “There is no way residents of Abuja will see the kind of infrastructure we have provided and say they are not happy with the achievements of Mr President. It is second to none,” he said. The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that the minister inspected the ongoing construction of Innet Southern Motorway, from the Area 1 roundabout to the Games Village bridges and Southern Parkway, linking Oladipo Diya Road with Ring Road II. He also inspected the ongoing construction of the Arterial Road S1 project in Abuja to connect Ring Road II to the FCT Fire Service Station in the Kaura and Gaduwa district corridors. Highlighting the rapid speed of execution on several key projects in the territory, Wike referenced the rapid transformation of the Southern Parkway project, which was flagged during the celebration of Tinubu’s third year in office. “Within six to seven months, you can see what has been achieved. “It is unimaginable, and that is why we are very happy,” Wike said. He pledged that the FCT administration remained on track to inaugurate at least 10 high-impact projects before the general elections scheduled for Jan. 16, 2027. item.title: Zamfara APC crisis deepens as aspirant petitions NEC, security agencies
item.description: …Yilwatda dismisses allegations as unfounded By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA — The crisis in the Zamfara State chapter of the All Progressives Congress (APC) has taken a fresh turn, following a petition by an aspirant to the party’s National Executive Committee (NEC), National Working Committee (NWC) and security agencies over the composition of a committee to conduct a court-ordered fresh primary election. The primary is for the Kaura Namoda/Birnin Magaji Federal Constituency following an order by the Court of Appeal. The aspirant, Honourable Hassan Umar Dangaladima, accused the party’s National Chairman, Prof. Nentawe Yilwatda, of unilaterally constituting the committee without involving the NWC. He alleged that the committee’s composition raised concerns about its impartiality and called on the party leadership to review the arrangement before the fresh primary. In the petition, Dangaladima claimed that no NWC meeting was convened to deliberate on or approve the committee’s composition and that neither the aspirants nor the Zamfara State chapter and other relevant stakeholders were consulted. However, Yilwatda, through his Special Adviser on Media and Strategic Communication, Abimbola Tooki, dismissed the allegations as unfounded. He said the claims did not reflect the party’s established decision-making process, insisting that the NWC operated as a collective body. “The National Chairman does not operate in isolation. He works in consultation and collaboration with other members of the NWC, and decisions are taken collectively in accordance with the party’s constitution, established procedures and internal mechanisms,” Tooki said. He described the suggestion that Yilwatda single-handedly constituted the committee without the knowledge or involvement of the NWC as misleading. According to him, the APC remains committed to respecting the rule of law, implementing court directives and ensuring that its internal processes are transparent, fair and credible. “The APC is a democratic institution governed by rules and collective responsibility, not the personal preferences of any individual,” he said. Alleges committee bias Dangaladima, however, maintained that the committee’s composition raised concerns about a possible conflict of interest. He alleged that some members were loyalists, supporters or agents of another aspirant, Honourable Aminu Sani Jaji, whom he described as his main rival in the contest. The petitioner also challenged Jaji’s eligibility, alleging that his name was not contained in the APC membership register for Birnin Magaji Ward submitted to the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). He said he obtained a Certified True Copy of the register from INEC, which he attached to his petition as evidence.
